question: Under identical existing-host policy, do native project-local skills improve fixed-task outcomes or observed scope adherence?
primary_metric: Five externally checkable tasks: complete task-run outcome passes / 15 scheduled trials per condition; separately report known denominator and infrastructure errors.
secondary_metrics: Per-task outcome passes / 3 scheduled trials per condition
Observed required/forbidden native skill reads; missing reads unknown, not success
manual_review: readonly-analysis answer: identifies percentage scaling and proposes discount_percent / 100 without implementation; separate from code outcome rate
python-tdd raw trace: test file edit, meaningful assertion failure, implementation edit, passing tests; observed sequence only, automated TDD remains unknown
decision_rule: Report zero or negative observed effect unchanged. Measurement completion is not evidence of a positive effect. No unplanned favorable prompt/grader edits after inspecting results.
limits: Existing host global AGENTS and managed policy may remain common to both arms; conditional project-skill effect, not pristine Vanilla.
Native project-local skill loading, not plugin installation/runtime effect.
Six fixed scenarios are exploratory, not proof of 41-skill population quality or a universal A+ score.
Prompts already prescribe several correct behaviors; ceiling effects are possible.
No actual Claude effect claim without authenticated Claude trials.
grading_boundary: Host Codex model; external checks in an existing reviewed network-disabled Docker container without credentials, with read-only workspace/checks.
pilot_exclusion: An initial run was stopped for grader isolation repair, not outcome selection; its artifacts remain separately marked aborted. Final matrix starts fresh with the same frozen inputs.
